contrasts.name: HOXA1_KD_vs_scramble
contrasts.evidence: GEO HiSeq sample titles match Lung_Scramble and Lung_A1KD in the result. Cuffdiff defines log2FC as sample_2/sample_1. All 11,605 OK rows with positive expression and finite FC agree with log2(value_2/value_1) within 1e-4. Keep the sign.

contrasts.name: INSR_KD_vs_scramble
contrasts.evidence: Result labels are Scr_KD then IR_KD, matching GEO shScr and shIR samples. Cuffdiff therefore reports IR/Scr. 20,278 of 20,279 OK finite positive-expression rows agree numerically within 1e-4. ENSG00000228252.4 (COL6A4P2) has an inconsistent magnitude but the same positive direction; retain the author coefficient 0.803023 and q=0.479485 without correction. Keep the sign.

contrasts.name: AM580_vs_DMSO_day6
contrasts.evidence: GEO sample titles explicitly map day-6 DMSO to q1 and day-6 AM580 to q3. The q1/q3 row block is present in the complete file. All 29,202 OK finite positive-expression rows in that block agree with log2(value_2/value_1) within 1e-4. Keep the sign; other row blocks are recorded separately and are not pooled.

contrasts.name: set2_KO_vs_WT
contrasts.evidence: GEO processing states SET2 KO against WT. In the same author table, mean SET2 FPKM is 0.682090 in KO versus 12.601670 in WT, with FC=-3.155502; YOR383C is 469.670022 versus 44.293420, with FC=+3.126276. 5,347/5,438 eligible matched genes agree in sign with supplied group FPKM means. These means only corroborate coefficient direction; author statistics are unchanged. Keep KO/WT.

contrasts.name: cord_blood_vs_adult
contrasts.evidence: The paper Results/Fig.4 explicitly reports HBG1, HBG2 and HBZ as higher in cord-blood-derived RNA-seq samples than adult-derived samples (https://doi.org/10.1002/ajh.24805). The author table has HBG1 logFC=+4.752799 and HBG2=+4.245726, with adult globins HBB=-0.712425 and HBD=-0.586473. This establishes CB/adult; keep the sign. Use adj.P.Val, never P.Value.

contrasts.name: old_vs_adult
contrasts.evidence: Use gene_exp_oldYoung_, not oldMid_. Its actual row labels are old then young. GEO Young1-3 have ages 5.5-8.5 months (adult in paper Table 1); VeryYoung1-3 are 3 months. Supplied sample FPKMs corroborate the mapping: cldn19 adult samples are 9.03982/7.11362/8.12401 versus 3-month samples 3.71964/2.54407/2.82978; the result young value is 11.6416 whereas the separate mid value is 4.17238. The oldYoung table reports adult/old, so flip to old/adult. All 15,175 OK finite positive-expression rows agree with value_2/value_1 within 1e-4.

contrasts.name: Tcf1_Lef1_DKO_vs_WT
contrasts.evidence: The table labels WT_0h then DKO_0h, matching GEO WT and Tcf1/Lef1-deficient samples. All 11,197 OK finite positive-expression rows match sample_2/sample_1 within 1e-4. Keep DKO/WT.

contrasts.name: mfl1_vs_Col0
contrasts.evidence: The selected table block explicitly labels Col0 then mfl1; the selected GEO samples have exactly these genotypes and Description=RNA-seq. All 22,809 OK finite positive-expression rows match sample_2/sample_1 within 1e-4. Keep mfl1/Col0. mfl1 is retained as the deposited label; no inferred gene-name replacement is used.

contrasts.name: Top1_Mut1_vs_WT_day15
contrasts.evidence: The selected worksheet is neuron.Mut.1vsWT_day15. Author-supplied per-sample RSEM TPMs confirm mutant/WT: Rasgrf1 means are 0.32/56.075 with FC=-7.282875; Peg13 means are 103.41/25.735 with FC=+2.016282. 16,068/16,519 matched eligible rows and all top 200 matched rows by padj agree with mutant/WT. Only exact label_label identifiers were matched for this diagnostic, without changing reference gene labels or statistics. Keep the sign.

files.duplicate_review: The author XLSX stores these gene cells as Excel date-formatted numbers (numFmtId 16), producing repeated raw IDs. They are retained as stored strings, not repaired or converted. One row has missing padj; the eligible duplicated IDs rank 631-633 in the positive direction at K=100 and cannot affect either top-100 list. All other numeric/date-like IDs were also checked to be outside the selected lists.

contrasts.name: MeiP26_KD_vs_bam
contrasts.evidence: File row labels are bam then bam_KD_meiP26, explicitly matching the two selected GEO genotypes. All 10,160 OK finite positive-expression rows agree with sample_2/sample_1 within 1e-4. Keep RNAi/bam.

files.duplicate_review: Two different author test_id values, Chd64 and P32, share gene_id=Chd64 and the same locus but have opposite coefficients. No row is selected as representative and no ID is replaced by test_id. Both rows remain in ranking: positive rank 438 and negative rank 1198, outside top100. Any K that brings this ambiguous ID into an answer is blocked.

files.id_type: Original R row names / gene labels

contrasts.name: Suz12_KO_vs_WT_ESC
contrasts.evidence: The selected ESC samples explicitly point to CTRL_SUZ12KO_stats_paired.txt in GEO, not the A-2 neural-progenitor result. Author code _Code/Fig6/Main_Panels_Fig6.qmd imports this exact CTRL_SUZ12KO file with invert_l2FC=FALSE and labels positive coefficients UP in Suz12 KO (lines 92-105,918-926). Source: https://github.com/Ni-Ar/SUZ12_AS/blob/e8af7d4959a0be668308fdaae8be647506e70c4c/_Code/Fig6/Main_Panels_Fig6.qmd. Keep KO/WT.

contrasts.name: Lonp1_KO_vs_control
contrasts.evidence: Paper Figure 4A explicitly reports Foxa1, Foxa2, Shh, Ptch1, Ptch2, Hhip and Etv5 lower in mutant lungs, and Fgf10, Etv4, Bmp4 and Id2 higher (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12490049/). All 11 signs match the q1/q2 table, identifying q1=control and q2=mutant. All 15,445 OK finite positive-expression rows match sample_2/sample_1 within 1e-4. Keep mutant/control.

files.id_type: Author gene labels in the unnamed first column

contrasts.name: siOGT_vs_siControl
contrasts.evidence: GEO defines paired siOGT and control experiments. Author count tables corroborate siOGT/control: OGT means 862.333333/3869.666667 with FC=-2.185610; NR1D1 means 12931.333333/4261.333333 with FC=+1.578348. 12,196/12,535 matched eligible genes and all top 200 matched rows by padj have this orientation. Means are only a diagnostic, not a replacement for paired-model coefficients. Keep the sign.

files.id_type: Author gene labels in the unnamed first column

contrasts.name: Sun1_KO_vs_control_tumors
contrasts.evidence: GEO processing explicitly describes the result as WT vs KO. Author RSEM TPMs confirm control/KO: Sun1 means in KO/control are 16.495714/54.37 yet FC=+1.508401; Ift81 means are 41.14/12.12875 yet FC=-2.288037. All top 200 matched rows by padj oppose KO/control means (16,386/20,209 across matched eligible rows). Flip the entire coefficient to KO/control; preserve coefficients and P values otherwise, including rows where simple means differ from the model.

contrasts.name: Sox10_KO_vs_control
contrasts.evidence: The paper describes myelin-gene reduction in Sox10 mutants (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11354551/). Corresponding author coefficients are negative: Mbp ENSMUSG00000041607=-0.537210, Aspa ENSMUSG00000020774=-1.612690, Ugt8a ENSMUSG00000032854=-1.475412. The top 200 matched rows by padj also agree with KO/control means of author counts. Gene labels were used only to check direction; reference IDs remain the original GeneID values. Keep KO/control; do not infer direction from filename order.

contrasts.name: hydrogel_0p7mM_vs_unembedded
contrasts.evidence: Use the concentration-effect author code, whose sample plan places 96wp as the first/reference condition. step2-multi_DESeq2.R takes that reference, labels output my.value vs ref.value and preserves factor order; RNAseqFunctions.R exports the resulting DESeq2 coefficients unchanged. Source: https://github.com/lldelisle/allRNAseqScriptsFromPineauWongNgEtAl2025. Thus Condition_Emb_0.7mMvs96wp_l2fc is embedding/control; keep the sign. The similarly named repository in GEO processing is a typo; use the paper Data Availability URL.
